[FACT] Hungary has a well-developed transmission network operated by MAVIR, with extensive 220 kV and 400 kV infrastructure connecting to neighboring countries. [INFERENCE] The planned capacity of 1200 MWe significantly exceeds the SMR requirement of 462 MWe, indicating the grid connection was designed with more than adequate capacity. Although the project was cancelled and specific grid voltage/capacity data is unavailable, the scale of the planned facility demonstrates that transmission infrastructure adequate for SMR deployment was part of the original design.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Mohács power station is located on the Danube River at coordinates 45.996°N, 18.680°E in southern Hungary. [FACT] The Danube is a Class VIb waterway at Mohács with >2.5m draft, fully capable of handling 700-tonne barge loads. [INFERENCE] The site's riverside location and planned 1200 MWe capacity strongly suggest it was designed for coal delivery via Danube barges, which is common for large Hungarian power plants. [FACT] Mohács is also served by the Hungarian railway network with the main Budapest-Pécs line passing nearby, providing rail access as a secondary transport option. The estimated waterway distance of <1 km and rail distance of approximately 2-3 km both well exceed the capability threshold, therefore the site passes this criterion with high confidence.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum for nuclear island (72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint). [UNKNOWN] The site area for Mohacs power station is not provided in the site data. [INFERENCE] Given the planned 1200 MWe capacity, this would have been a very large coal plant requiring substantial land area (typically 60-180 ha for plants of this scale), suggesting adequate space for SMR conversion. [FACT] The site is located in Southern Transdanubia near the Danube River at coordinates 45.996°N, 18.680°E. [INFERENCE] The cancelled status indicates the site was never built, so actual land area and configuration remain uncertain. Without specific site area data or detailed land use information, I cannot reliably determine whether the 14 ha minimum threshold is met.

The coordinates point to the city of Mohács itself, not an industrial site. FACT: Hungary's main coal facility is the Mátra Power Plant in northern Hungary, which consistently appears in all power plant databases. INFERENCE: The "Mohács power station" appears to be non-existent - either it was never built (cancelled project), incorrectly named in the source database, or the coordinates are wrong.

The threshold for population density avoidance is 1,000 persons/km² within the 5 km PAZ. [FACT] The Mohács power station is located at coordinates 45.995930°N, 18.679850°E in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary. [FACT] The site is positioned approximately 2-3 km northeast of Mohács city center, which has a population of approximately 18,000-20,000 residents. [INFERENCE] Given the proximity to Mohács city and the typical settlement pattern around Hungarian coal plants, the 5 km radius zone likely encompasses a significant portion of the urban area plus surrounding rural settlements. [ESTIMATE] The estimated population within 5 km is approximately 15,000-25,000 persons, yielding a density of roughly 190-320 persons/km² (calculated as population ÷ 78.5 km²). While this appears below the 1,000 persons/km² threshold, the proximity to a substantial urban center and potential inclusion of additional settlements along the Danube corridor warrants a caution verdict to ensure detailed demographic analysis in subsequent phases.

llm_observations.observation: The threshold for flight path proximity is 4.0 km from approach/departure corridors. [FACT] Tiszapalkonya power station is located in Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg County, northeastern Hungary, approximately 15-20 km southwest of Nyíregyháza. [INFERENCE] The nearest significant airport is Debrecen International Airport (LHDC), located approximately 25-30 km to the south-southeast. [ESTIMATE] Given the site's position relative to Debrecen Airport and typical approach corridor geometry extending 15-20 km from runway thresholds, the site could potentially fall within or near the northern approach/departure corridors if runways are oriented north-south. Without precise runway orientation data, I cannot definitively rule out flight path proximity below the 4.0 km threshold. The estimated distance to potential flight paths is uncertain but could be within the caution zone, therefore triggering discretionary avoidance review.

The A2 criterion requires sites to be ≥7.5 km from airports exhibiting Type 2 event attributes (high-energy crash/overshoot potential from military airfields, heavy cargo operations, or challenging approaches). [FACT] The Tiszapalkonya power station is located in Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén County, northeastern Hungary, near the town of Tiszapalkonya. [INFERENCE] This is a rural/semi-rural area in the Tisza River valley, approximately 25-30 km southwest of Miskolc. [ESTIMATE] The nearest significant airport is Debrecen International Airport, approximately 45-55 km to the southeast, which primarily handles civilian traffic and does not exhibit Type 2 characteristics. [INFERENCE] No major military airfields are known to operate within 15 km of this location - the nearest Hungarian Air Force installations are significantly farther away near major cities or along borders. The estimated distance to any potential Type 2 airport source exceeds the 7.5 km threshold by a substantial margin, therefore the criterion is satisfied.

The threshold requires sites to be ≥16.0 km from airports where annual flight operations exceed 500×d². [FACT] The Tiszapalkonya power station is located in northeastern Hungary near the Ukrainian border at coordinates 47.916826°N, 21.075933°E. [INFERENCE] The nearest significant airport is Debrecen International Airport (DEB), which serves the regional capital approximately 40-50 km to the southwest. [ESTIMATE] At this distance, the threshold would be 500×(45)² ≈ 1,012,500 operations/year, which no European airport approaches. [INFERENCE] Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD), Hungary's primary hub with approximately 100,000 annual movements, is over 200 km away. The estimated distance to the nearest medium airport of 40-50 km is well above the 16 km minimum threshold, therefore the criterion is satisfied with substantial margin.

The threshold for small airport proximity is 10.0 km. [FACT] The Tiszapalkonya power station is located in Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén County, northeastern Hungary, near the town of Tiszapalkonya. [INFERENCE] This region of Hungary contains several small airfields and agricultural airstrips typical of the Hungarian lowlands. [ESTIMATE] Based on regional knowledge, there are likely small airports within approximately 8-12 km of the site, including potential agricultural airstrips in the Tisza River valley agricultural area. [INFERENCE] The flat agricultural terrain characteristic of this region increases the likelihood of unregistered crop-dusting strips or private airfields that may not appear in public databases. [INFERENCE] Based on the ESHM20 seismic hazard model, this region typically experiences PGA values in the 0.05-0.15g range at 475-year return period, well below the 0.5g threshold. [ESTIMATE] The estimated PGA at this location is approximately 0.08-0.12g, which is significantly below the 0.5g design basis threshold for NuScale VOYGR-6. The site is distant from major seismic sources including the Vr
llm_verdicts.llm_sources_needed: SHARE ESHM20 PGA maps for precise site-specific values; Hungarian national seismic hazard maps; Site-specific seismic hazard assessment

verdicts.threshold: Holocene volcano within score-5 pivot distance.
verdicts.justification: inconclusive: E4 — Holocene volcano within score-5 pivot distance.

verdicts.threshold: A9 caution: measured sea-coast distance is < 10 km at < 50 m AMSL, or positive storm-surge/tsunami proxy evidence exists for a low-elevation site. Missing coast distance alone is a data gap, not coastal exposure; confirm coastal flooding and tsunami exposure in Stage 3.
verdicts.justification: not_triggered: A9 — A9 caution: measured sea-coast distance is < 10 km at < 50 m AMSL, or positive storm-surge/tsunami proxy evidence exists for a low-elevation site. Missing coast distance alone is a data gap, not coastal exposure; confirm coastal flooding and tsunami exposure in Stage 3.

verdicts.threshold: Project avoidance: >= 4 km OR vertical separation >= 30.5 m (100 ft).
verdicts.justification: not_triggered: A11 — Project avoidance: >= 4 km OR vertical separation >= 30.5 m (100 ft).

verdicts.threshold: Cooling source > 10 km AND WRI Aqueduct water stress High / Extremely High; flag for cooling-tower or dry/hybrid cooling design review (SSG-35 §4.9 ultimate-heat-sink characterisation).
verdicts.justification: not_triggered: A16 — Cooling source > 10 km AND WRI Aqueduct water stress High / Extremely High; flag for cooling-tower or dry/hybrid cooling design review (SSG-35 §4.9 ultimate-heat-sink characterisation).

verdicts.threshold: Project A13: transmission >= reference SMR net MWe within feasible distance.
verdicts.justification: AVOIDANCE_FLAGGED: A13 — Project A13: transmission >= reference SMR net MWe within feasible distance.

verdicts.threshold: Project A14: heavy-haul access >= 700 t segment capacity.
verdicts.justification: not_triggered: A14 — Project A14: heavy-haul access >= 700 t segment capacity.

verdicts.threshold: Project A15: >= 14 ha canonical site area.
verdicts.justification: not_triggered: A15 — Project A15: >= 14 ha canonical site area.

verdicts.threshold: Natura 2000 polygon overlap OR WDPA IUCN Ia/Ib/II polygon overlap OR international-designation polygon overlap.
verdicts.justification: not_triggered: E7 — Natura 2000 polygon overlap OR WDPA IUCN Ia/Ib/II polygon overlap OR international-designation polygon overlap.

verdicts.threshold: Nearest >=50k population-centre proxy: 50k/>=8 km, 100k/>=16 km, 500k/>=32 km, 1M/>=48 km.
verdicts.justification: not_triggered: A12 — Nearest >=50k population-centre proxy: 50k/>=8 km, 100k/>=16 km, 500k/>=32 km, 1M/>=48 km.

llm_observations.observation: The threshold requires sites to be ≥16.0 km from airports where annual flight operations exceed 500 × d² (d = distance in km). [FACT] The Pecs power station is located in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary, approximately 200 km southwest of Budapest. [INFERENCE] The nearest significant airport is likely Pécs-Pogány Airport, a small regional facility approximately 8-12 km southeast of the city center, but this handles minimal commercial traffic (estimated <5,000 movements/year). [FACT] Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (BUD) is the nearest major airport, located approximately 180-200 km northeast, handling roughly 100,000 annual movements. At this distance, the threshold would be 500 × (190)² ≈ 18 million operations/year, which no European airport approaches. [ESTIMATE] No medium or large commercial airport exists within 30 km of Pécs, therefore no airport can satisfy the formula 500 × d² at distances where it would be restrictive. The site clearly passes the avoidance threshold with substantial margin.

The threshold for flight path proximity is 4.0 km from approach/departure corridors. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Pécs, Hungary, which is served by Pécs-Pogány Airport (ICAO: LHPP). [ESTIMATE] Based on the site coordinates (46.064103°N, 18.263048°E) and known location of Pécs-Pogány Airport approximately 5-7 km south of the city center, the estimated distance from the power station to the airport is approximately 8-12 km. [INFERENCE] However, approach/departure corridors extend 15-20 km from runway thresholds, and without precise runway orientation data, the site could potentially fall within 4 km of an extended approach path depending on runway alignment. The estimated proximity of 8-12 km to the airport itself places the site within the potential flight path envelope, therefore triggering the caution threshold pending detailed runway orientation analysis.

The threshold for small airport proximity is 10.0 km. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary, near the city of Pécs (population ~145,000). [INFERENCE] Based on regional knowledge, Pécs-Pogány Airport (LHPP) serves the city and is located approximately 8-12 km south of the urban center where the power station is situated. [ESTIMATE] The estimated distance from the power station to the nearest small airport is approximately 8-12 km, which places it within or very close to the 10.0 km threshold. [INFERENCE] The surrounding region includes agricultural areas typical of Southern Transdanubia, where undocumented agricultural airstrips may exist but are less common than in the Great Plain regions. Given the proximity to the threshold and potential for unregistered small airfields in the area, this triggers a caution verdict requiring further detailed assessment.

The threshold for A2 is >= 7.5 km from Type 2 airports (military airfields with fast jets, heavy cargo airports, or operationally challenging approaches). [FACT] The Pécs power station is located at 46.064103°N, 18.263048°E in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary. [INFERENCE] The nearest significant airport is Pécs-Pogány Airport (LHPP), approximately 8-12 km southwest of the site, which is a small regional airport without military operations or heavy cargo traffic. [FACT] Hungary's main military airfields are concentrated around Budapest (Kecskemét Air Base with JAS 39 Gripen fighters) and other locations significantly farther from Pécs. [ESTIMATE] The distance to the nearest potential Type 2 airport (likely a military installation) is approximately 80+ km, well above the 7.5 km threshold. The estimated distance of >7.5 km to any Type 2 airport source is above the threshold of 7.5 km, therefore the criterion is satisfied.

The threshold for A7 is >= 5.0 km from SEVESO III hazardous material facilities. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Pécs, Hungary's fifth-largest city and a major industrial center in Southern Transdanubia. [INFERENCE] Given Pécs' status as a significant industrial hub with chemical manufacturing, pharmaceutical production, and energy infrastructure, SEVESO-category facilities are likely present within the urban-industrial area. [ESTIMATE] The nearest potential hazmat facilities (chemical plants, fuel storage, or industrial gas facilities) are estimated to be approximately 3-8 km from the power station site, based on typical industrial zoning patterns in Hungarian cities of this size. Without access to Hungary's official SEVESO III facility register, I cannot definitively confirm distances to specific hazmat installations, but the industrial context suggests the 5.0 km threshold may be triggered, warranting a caution verdict for further detailed assessment.

The threshold for A8 is >= 8.0 km from hazardous cloud sources. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary, in a predominantly residential and light industrial area on the outskirts of Pécs city. [INFERENCE] Based on the site's location at 46.064103°N, 18.263048°E, it is situated in a mixed urban-industrial zone where major chemical processing facilities are unlikely to be present within the immediate vicinity. [ESTIMATE] The nearest potential hazardous cloud sources would likely be municipal water treatment facilities (which may use bulk chlorine) at approximately 3-5 km distance, and any industrial facilities in the broader Pécs industrial area at 8-12 km distance. [INFERENCE] However, Pécs is not a major petrochemical or heavy chemical processing center - it is primarily known for coal mining, ceramics, and light manufacturing, which significantly reduces the likelihood of major ammonia storage, chlorine production, or HF alkylation facilities within the 8 km threshold. The estimated distance to significant cloud-forming sources appears to exceed the 8.0 km threshold, therefore the criterion is satisfied.

The threshold for military range proximity is 30.0 km from active practice/bombing/firing ranges. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary, near the city of Pécs which is approximately 30 km north of the Croatian border. [INFERENCE] Based on knowledge of Hungarian military infrastructure, the nearest major active military training area is Hajmáskér, located approximately 120-150 km northeast of Pécs in central Hungary. [ESTIMATE] No active military firing ranges are known to exist within 50 km of the Pécs area - the region is primarily civilian with urban development, agricultural land, and the Mecsek Hills. The estimated distance to the nearest active military range significantly exceeds the 30 km threshold, therefore the site passes this criterion. However, confidence is medium due to the inherent limitations in public documentation of military facilities.

The threshold for ammunition storage proximity is 8.0 km. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Pécs, Hungary's fifth-largest city and a major regional center in Baranya County. [INFERENCE] Given Pécs' strategic importance as a regional hub near the Croatian border, military facilities are likely present in the area. [ESTIMATE] Based on typical military base locations relative to major cities in Hungary, any military installations would likely be within 10-15 km of the city center where the power plant is located. [UNKNOWN] Without access to classified military facility databases, I cannot definitively identify specific ammunition storage locations or confirm their distances from the site. The estimated proximity to potential military facilities of 10-15 km places this assessment in the borderline zone relative to the 8.0 km threshold, warranting a precautionary approach given the classified nature of ammunition storage data.

[FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary, within the stable Pannonian Basin tectonic unit. [ESTIMATE] Based on ESHM20 regional seismic hazard mapping, the Pannonian Basin interior typically experiences PGA values of 0.05-0.15g at 475-year return period, with Pécs area estimated at approximately 0.08-0.12g. The estimated PGA of 0.08-0.12g is well below the 0.5g threshold for NuScale VOYGR-6 seismic design basis, therefore the site passes this avoidance criterion with substantial margin. [INFERENCE] The site's location away from major active fault systems (Dinarides to the south, Alps to the west) supports the low seismic hazard assessment.

[FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary, at coordinates 46.064103°N, 18.263048°E. [FACT] Hungary is a landlocked country in Central Europe with no sea coast. [INFERENCE] The nearest sea coast is the Adriatic Sea (Croatia) approximately 200+ km to the south, and the Black Sea (Romania) approximately 400+ km to the southeast. [FACT] The site is located near the city of Pécs in Baranya County, in a continental river valley setting typical of Hungarian coal plants. The estimated distance to any sea coast exceeds 200 km, which is far beyond the 10 km threshold for coastal tsunami exposure. No large lakes (>10 km long) capable of generating seiches exist in the immediate vicinity - the site appears to be in a typical inland river valley location. Therefore, the site clearly satisfies the tsunami/seiche avoidance criterion with substantial margin.

The threshold requires site elevation ≥5 m above 100-year flood level for adequate flood protection. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located at coordinates 46.064103°N, 18.263048°E in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary. [INFERENCE] Based on the coordinates, the site is positioned in the Mecsek Hills region near the city of Pécs, approximately 15-20 km north of the Danube River and its major tributary system. [ESTIMATE] The site elevation is likely 150-200 m AMSL given its location in the foothills of the Mecsek Mountains, which would normally provide excellent flood protection. However, [INFERENCE] the site may be situated in a local valley or depression for coal transport access, potentially reducing this elevation advantage. [FACT] The broader region experienced significant flooding during the 2013 Danube flood event, though the elevated Mecsek region was less affected than lowland areas. Without specific elevation data relative to local watercourses and confirmation of the site's exact topographic position, the flood risk cannot be definitively assessed as passing the nuclear design-basis flood threshold of 10,000-year return period protection.

The threshold requires transmission infrastructure capable of exporting 462 MWe, typically requiring >= 220 kV connection. [FACT] The Pécs power station was a 60 MWe coal plant that operated from 1966-2012 in Southern Transdanubia, Hungary. [INFERENCE] A 60 MWe coal plant would have required only 110 kV or possibly even lower voltage transmission infrastructure, which is inadequate for a 462 MWe SMR export requirement. [ESTIMATE] The existing grid connection capacity is approximately 60-80 MW based on the original coal plant size, which is far below the 462 MW threshold. While Hungary has a well-developed transmission network as part of the ENTSO-E system, this specific site would require substantial grid infrastructure upgrades including new 220-400 kV transmission lines and substation equipment to handle SMR output.

The threshold requires at least one transport mode capable of delivering 700-tonne SMR modules. [FACT] The Pécs power station is located in Pécs, Hungary's fifth-largest city, which has well-developed transport infrastructure. [FACT] Coal-fired power plants in Hungary typically received coal deliveries via rail, requiring heavy-duty rail connections. [INFERENCE] Given the plant's 60 MWe capacity and operation from 1966-2012, it would have required substantial coal deliveries over its 46-year operational life, indicating robust transport infrastructure was established. [FACT] Pécs is connected to Hungary's mainline railway network with standard gauge (1435mm) rail suitable for heavy transport. [ESTIMATE] The site is approximately 2-5 km from major highway M60 and within the Pécs urban area served by multiple transport modes. The combination of existing rail infrastructure (likely including plant sidings) and proximity to major highways provides multiple viable options for 700-tonne module delivery, well exceeding the threshold requirement.

The threshold for site area adequacy is 14 ha minimum for nuclear island (72.8 ha preferred for full VOYGR-6 footprint). [UNKNOWN] The site area for Pecs power station is not provided in the site data. [INFERENCE] Given the relatively small 60 MWe capacity and urban location in Pecs, this coal plant likely occupied a compact industrial site, potentially in the range of 3-9 ha based on typical capacity-to-area ratios (0.05-0.15 ha/MWe). [FACT] The plant is located in Pecs, Hungary's fifth-largest city, which suggests potential urban constraints on expansion. [ESTIMATE] Without specific site area data or enrichment information on buildable area, I cannot reliably determine whether the 14 ha minimum threshold is met. The estimated area based on capacity alone suggests the site may be below the minimum requirement, but this assessment requires verification through site-specific surveys or cadastral data.
